answer.verdict: Sony libsd clears SPU2 ATTR bit 6 before the user handler; the zsiopdrv worker re-arms with sceSdSetCoreAttr(core 1, SD_CORE_IRQ_ENABLE, 1) after moving IRQA. The leave-enable workaround is removed. The post-handler ready-thread pump runs that re-arm before later samples. Airport music and fight fps hold.

facts.c: PCSX2 Mixer fires the IRQ only while IRQEnable is set and does not clear that bit. Sony libsd Spu2Interrupt (freesd and Tekken's SDK 2.4.3 module) reads IRQINFO 0xBF9007C2 bits 2..3, writes ATTR & 0xFFBF on the fired core (core0 0xBF90019A, core1 0xBF90059A), then calls the user handler.

PCSX2 savestate slot 02 (character select) core1 IRQEnable=1 IRQA=0xdc000 (byte 0x1B8000), voice 20 NextA already past IRQA. Slot 01 core1 IRQEnable=1 IRQA=0xdc080. Core0 IRQEnable=0 IRQA=0x800 in both. The cleared window is shorter than a savestate.
takeSpu2Irq now clears the latch and ATTR bit 6 before the user handler. setCoreAttr case 4 already applies SD_CORE_IRQ_ENABLE to bit 6. getCoreAttr(4/5) returns that bit.

If the fired core is still disabled after the handler, serviceSpu2Irq runs up to 24 ready slices (beginNextReady, runCpu(kDefaultSlice), endTimeslice) with m_inSpu2Irq set so drainMixedAudio cannot re-enter, then continues advanceTo. A full pump is 6144 IOP cycles, about 8 samples.

In logs/grok/spu2irq-1 every logged re-arm is pump=1 inirq=0. Pattern per cross: coreattr entry=5 val=0 ra=4bc58, setAddr IRQA entry=1f01 val=1b8000 or 1b8100 ra=4c110, coreattr entry=5 val=1 ra=4c69c. No inirq=1 and no stubbed libsd ordinal. Last counters n=16128 attrOn=5376 attrOff=5376 irqa=5376, still paired.

irqHits moves: 217 at mix=5, 2431 at mix=50, 3661 at mix=75, 4891 at mix=100, 5383 at mix=110 (about 49/s). irqa stays 0/dc000. Core1 ATTR bit 6 is set at every 5 s sample (attr 40c0 then 4040 after effect off). maxAdv stays 2605 because that field is a max from boot, not a steady-state counter.

Music sceCdRead continues: lsn 1070970 sectors=64 dst=0x160000, then 0x180000 and 0x1a0000, then 32-sector steps across 0x160000-0x1a0000. A second stream at lsn 1112416 is still stepping those destinations at mix=110 (lsn 1113568).

fix.change: Clear ATTR bit 6 when taking the latched IRQ, matching libsd's ANDI 0xFFBF before the user handler. Drop the leave-enable workaround.

After the handler, if a fired core's IRQ enable is still clear, run up to 24 ready IOP slices so the worker's sceSdSetCoreAttr(SD_CORE_IRQ_ENABLE, 1) lands before advanceTo plays past the next IRQA. m_inSpu2Irq blocks a nested drain.
TEKKEN4_LIBSD_LOG=1 (exact) logs ordinal 11 entry 4 and setAddr id 0x1F: first 48 lines, then every 256th, with ra, inirq, pump, and running attrOn/attrOff/irqa counts.

contra: Hardware does not clear IRQEnable. The clear is Sony libsd. Our HLE is the library, so clearing the bit is the match.
Savestates show the enable already back on. They do not show the few-microsecond cleared window. The runtime log shows val=0 then val=1 on every cross.

Every logged re-arm has pump=1 because the worker is first run from the pump after the handler's semaphore signal. That does not mean the normal scheduler could not also run it; the pump is what makes a large catch-up safe.

Fight rms t=90..100 (0.146-0.250) is quieter than excerpt_fight_80s's first seconds (0.295-0.311) and ends near that excerpt's last second (0.180). irqHits and sceCdRead do not stall, so this is level, not a stopped stream.
52 clipped samples, peak from a -32768 in t=22..29 (menu), not the fight.
Perf is 59-61 in the fight window, not a literal 60 on seconds 81, 83, and 85.
